title: Amen Thompson Signs $208M Extension with Rockets
seoTitle: Amen Thompson Signs $208M Extension with Rockets
subtitle: The five-year renewal includes a trade kicker clause and keeps the young standout in Houston through 2032
excerpt: Amen Thompson, 23, has signed a five-year, $208 million contract with the Houston Rockets, reinforcing the franchise's strategy to lock down its young core.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Amen Thompson's signing of a five-year, $208 million extension has placed the player among the few NBA rookies to secure a multi-million-dollar deal right in his early seasons.

Extension Details

The agreement, reported by Shams Charania on ESPN, runs through 2032 and includes a 10% trade bonus clause. The extension keeps the guard under contract with the Houston Rockets for nearly a decade.

Performance Justifying the Investment

Selected as the fourth overall pick in the 2023 Draft, Thompson averaged 18.3 points, 5.3 assists, and 1.5 steals this past season. He led the NBA in minutes played and ranked among the leaders in steals and loose balls recovered.

Versatility on the Court

With the absence of Fred VanVleet, Thompson played primarily as a point guard, but demonstrated the ability to play every perimeter position and even inside the paint. His adaptability allows the head coach to adjust the lineup as needed.

Ranking Among the League's Best

Last season, Thompson joined the elite group of nine players who averaged at least 18 points, seven rebounds, and five assists, alongside names like Nikola Jokic, Luka Doncic, Giannis Antetokounmpo, and Jayson Tatum.

Rockets' Strategy for the Future

Thompson's renewal follows other recent franchise extensions, such as those of Alperen Şengün, Jabari Smith Jr., and Tari Eason, in addition to the presence of Kevin Durant. The club aims to solidify its young core and ensure salary stability for the coming years.

Other Rookies Seeking Similar Deals

Following Thompson's extension, other players from the 2023 draft class, such as Victor Wembanyama, had already signed similar contracts. Names like Brandon Miller, Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George, Cason Wallace, Jaime Jaquez Jr., and Brandin Podziemski are also pointed out as potential candidates for high-value agreements.

With information from MARCA.
